study.question: Does independent control of the auxiliary-only feedback extension context-input and reused query-weight gradients recover click quality without losing its auxiliary gains, and can any cell exceed the incumbent at measured cost?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g0-r0081-feedback_aux_only has click AUC0.667352987 versus incumbent0.668531811 while auxiliary AUCs improve from0.803864/0.814572/0.828078 to0.825919/0.846806/0.845552. Removing direct click readout improved on feedback_all_tasks0.666275380 but left a0.001178824 click gap. Its extension still updates shared context embeddings and per-aux-task query weights reused by the inherited history adapter. These two gradient edges may interact to alter auxiliary transfer into context. Block each edge independently while preserving the forward function, summaries, extension trainability and capacity. This is a path-specific hypothesis, not established mediation or a new architecture claim.

nearest_work.difference: Immediate parent. Change only two auxiliary extension gradient edges; preserve task-aligned source, detached summary, disabled click extension and all learned state.
Prior context gate had click extension enabled and retained native query-weight gradients; current factorial tests both edges with click readout disabled.

Read pinned benchmark forward123..219: task-masked sequence hubs and iterative aggregation/broadcast. Inherit only the local task-mask-inspired covariance extension; no hub network is newly reproduced. This study tests branch-local optimization ownership.
Read exact-version archived primary text29..78 describing target-conditioned local activation; inherit adapted local activation and Dice, not exact original reproduction.
Original-paper link/provenance only; full text unavailable via authorized snapshot. Original novelty and equivalence remain unverified.

inherited_components: Complete g0-r0081-feedback_aux_only standalone module and frozen config except the two branch-edge switches.
DIN/action-aware local activation; ten-block uniform/feedback compression; target-match and ordinal/quadratic details; folded support and pruned eval.
Four task towers/residual adapters; blockwise product context-history interactions; inherited first-order buy-summary VJP.
Task-aligned common-support covariance extension; auxiliary summary detach; context-query projection reused by incumbent history branch; disabled click extension readout.
All module construction/initialization, parameters, buffers and RNG; native sum-four-BCE loss and host optimizers.
study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 gradient-edge factorial: block_aux_extension_context_grad controls only the extension context input; new block_aux_extension_query_weight_grad detaches only the reused query weight in extension F.linear. Both gates act only for auxiliary labels during training. Inherited uses of that same weight/context remain live. Inference and common-state train predictions unchanged; no extra learned state or optimizer intervention.
predictions: Blocking both edges should improve click AUC over attached0.667352987 if extension-specific transfer through these edges is harmful, while retaining auxiliary gains over incumbent; useful task progress additionally requires click above0.668531811.

Conditional query-weight and context-input effects will identify which path is useful to control; report both simple effects and the difference of differences on AUC without assuming loss-scale additivity.

All cells have identical common-state predictions, forward buffers, initialized learned state and registered capacity; only selected auxiliary extension VJPs differ. The attached replay should recover archived feedback_aux_only within host tolerances.

If query-weight effects emerge only with context edge enabled, shared projection changes may alter contextual transfer through other branches; without gradient telemetry this remains a provisional explanation.
falsifiers: No edge-blocked cell improves click over attached at unchanged source; then the claimed harmful-edge explanation lacks predictive support.
Blocked cells improve click only by erasing auxiliary gains, or remain below incumbent; then useful complementarity is not established.
A gain is reproduced by capacity/source alternatives or explained by measured extra cost in follow-up; then do not attribute it uniquely to feedback or efficiency.
Any common-state forward/buffer mismatch, incorrect isolated branch VJP, changed inherited gradient ownership, nonfinite backward or attached-parent parity failure blocks interpretation.
Different source-by-gate interactions, seed reversal, or user-cluster uncertainty can overturn a single-seed ranking.
alternative_explanations: Global dense gradient clipping changes all dense updates when extension gradients change. No clipping statistics were supplied.
Changed auxiliary logits alter gradients through inherited history/residual/tower paths even when the extension is detached from context/query; both-blocked is not full training isolation.
Restrictive common support, feedback/value scaling, label mismatch and single-pass optimization can explain failure independent of queried gradient paths.
Historical match_aux_only slightly outperformed feedback_aux_only; feedback-specific value is unsupported and not isolated by this factorial.

Early task-compressed variants underperformed the stronger source; later details improved quality. The current incumbent itself sacrifices auxiliary quality versus DIN. No one branch refutes the broad joint-model hypothesis.
Many adaptive trials at one seed induce selection bias; deterministic historical replays are not independent repetitions.
